Calculate sample size for a target margin of error when estimating prevalence

Source: R/design_precision.R
design_precision.Rd

Given a target precision (margin of error), returns the minimum total sample size required. Handles imperfect diagnostic tests via the Rogan-Gladen variance adjustment, and clustered sampling via the design effect (Kish formula).

Three design modes – controlled by n_sites and n_per_site:

Unclustered (n_sites = NULL, n_per_site = NULL)

Treats all observations as independent. Returns total n only.

Fixed site size (n_per_site supplied)

Solves for the number of sites.

Fixed number of sites (n_sites supplied)

Solves for the number of people per site.

Usage

design_precision(
  prevalence,
  moe,
  sensitivity = 1,
  specificity = 1,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  n_sites = NULL,
  n_per_site = NULL,
  icc = 0
)

Arguments

prevalence

Expected true prevalence, in (0, 1).

moe

Target margin of error (half-width of the confidence interval) on the true-prevalence scale, in (0, 0.5). A decimal fraction, e.g. 0.05 for +/-5 percentage points.

sensitivity

Diagnostic sensitivity in (0, 1]; default 1 (perfect test).

specificity

Diagnostic specificity in (0, 1]; default 1. sensitivity + specificity must exceed 1.

conf_level

Confidence level, in (0, 1); default 0.95.

n_sites

Optional whole number. Fixes the number of sites; the function solves for people per site. Cannot be used with n_per_site.

n_per_site

Optional whole number. Fixes the number of people per site; the function solves for the number of sites. Cannot be used with n_sites.

icc

Intra-cluster correlation, in [0, 1]; default 0 (no clustering). An icc above 0 needs n_sites or n_per_site.

Value

A list with:

n

Total sample size. With sites, n_sites * n_per_site.

n_sites

Number of sites (NULL if unclustered).

n_per_site

People per site (NULL if unclustered).

deff

Design effect of the returned design, 1 + (n_per_site - 1) * icc; 1 if unclustered.

n_eff

Unclustered sample size \(n_0\) that gives the same precision, rounded up.

Details

Rogan-Gladen variance adjustment: the Rogan-Gladen transform is linear in the apparent prevalence, so scaling its variance by the (constant) RG slope is exact – not a delta-method approximation. The unclustered sample size is

$$n_0 = \frac{z^2 \, p_{app}(1-p_{app})}{MOE^2 \cdot (Se + Sp - 1)^2}$$

where \(p_{app} = p \cdot Se + (1-p)(1-Sp)\) is the apparent prevalence implied by the expected true prevalence and the test characteristics. When \(Se = Sp = 1\) this reduces to the standard MOE formula.

Fixed site size: the design effect \(D_{eff} = 1 + (n_{per site} - 1) \cdot ICC\) is known directly, so \(n = n_0 \cdot D_{eff}\) and the number of sites is ceiling(n / n_per_site).

Fixed number of sites: Deff depends on the number of people per site, \(n / n_{sites}\), which depends on n. Substituting and solving gives the closed form:

$$n = \frac{n_0 \cdot n_{sites} \cdot (1-ICC)}{n_{sites} - n_0 \cdot ICC}$$

A solution exists only when \(n_{sites} > n_0 \cdot ICC\). Otherwise the target MOE is unachievable: each site is worth at most \(1/ICC\) independent people however many are sampled there, so the MOE floors at

$$MOE_{min} = z\sqrt{\frac{p_{app}(1-p_{app}) \cdot ICC} {n_{sites} \cdot (Se + Sp - 1)^2}}$$

and the function stops and reports this minimum.

Rounding: the number of sites (or people per site) is rounded up, and the returned n is the number actually sampled, n_sites * n_per_site, so it can be slightly above the continuous solution.

References

Rogan WJ, Gladen B (1978). Estimating prevalence from the results of a screening test. American Journal of Epidemiology 107(1):71-76.

MMS-SD Study Design Workshop, Modules 1 (sampling), 2 (sample size from margin of error) and 5 (ICC / design effect). https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMS-SD_workshop/

Examples

# Unclustered, perfect test
design_precision(prevalence = 0.3, moe = 0.05)
#> $n
#> [1] 323
#> 
#> $n_sites
#> NULL
#> 
#> $n_per_site
#> NULL
#> 
#> $deff
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 323
#> 

# Imperfect test (sensitivity 90%, specificity 95%)
design_precision(0.3, 0.05, sensitivity = 0.9, specificity = 0.95)
#> $n
#> [1] 451
#> 
#> $n_sites
#> NULL
#> 
#> $n_per_site
#> NULL
#> 
#> $deff
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 451
#> 

# Fixed site size: how many sites do I need?
design_precision(0.3, 0.05, n_per_site = 10, icc = 0.05)
#> $n
#> [1] 470
#> 
#> $n_sites
#> [1] 47
#> 
#> $n_per_site
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $deff
#> [1] 1.45
#> 
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 323
#> 

# Fixed number of sites: how many people per site?
design_precision(0.3, 0.05, n_sites = 50, icc = 0.05)
#> $n
#> [1] 500
#> 
#> $n_sites
#> [1] 50
#> 
#> $n_per_site
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $deff
#> [1] 1.45
#> 
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 323
#>
